title: India and International Organizations — A Consolidated View
shortDescription: Every India-specific fact from this subject, gathered in one place — founding memberships, hosted offices, and status types, neutral and factual.
genZNote: The India cheat-sheet: where India is a founder, where it's just a guest, and where it actually runs the building.

sections.heading: Where India Is a Founding Member
bullets: United Nations (1945) — India signed the Charter even before independence.
IMF and World Bank (1945/44) — founding member of both Bretton Woods institutions.
WHO (1948), UNESCO, WTO (1995, and an original GATT signatory from 1948), FAO, ILO, ICAO (1944).
SAARC (1985) and BIMSTEC (1997) — founding member of both South Asian regional groupings.
Asian Development Bank (1966) and, later, the New Development Bank (BRICS-founded, 2014/15).

sections.heading: Where India Joined Later (Not a Founder)
bullets: SCO — India became a full member only in 2017, alongside Pakistan, in the same expansion round (SCO itself was established in 2001).
AIIB — India is the largest borrower and second-largest shareholder (after China), though not a 'founder' in the same sense as a 1940s institution — AIIB itself only began operating in 2016.

sections.heading: Where India Is a Partner, Not a Member
bullets: ASEAN — Dialogue Partner and Strategic Partner, NOT a full member.
OECD — 'Key Partner' country, NOT a member.
European Union, Gulf Cooperation Council, African Union — Strategic Partnerships / cooperation frameworks, no membership category applies (India is not geographically part of any of these regions).
NATO — no formal relationship; India is not a member and is not seeking membership.

sections.heading: International Offices Hosted in India
bullets: WHO Regional Office for South-East Asia — New Delhi.
WHO Global Centre for Traditional Medicine — Jamnagar, Gujarat (established as a WHO knowledge hub for traditional medicine).

sections.heading: Contributions and Milestones
bullets: India has historically been among the largest troop- and police-contributing countries to UN peacekeeping operations, going back to the 1950s.
India accepted IMF conditional lending in 1991 during a severe balance-of-payments crisis — a pivotal moment that preceded India's economic liberalization reforms.
India was declared polio-free by WHO in 2014.
India hosted the G20 presidency in 2023 (New Delhi Summit), during which the African Union was admitted as a permanent G20 member.

India continues to seek permanent UN Security Council membership, primarily through the G4 grouping alongside Brazil, Germany, and Japan — this remains an aspiration, not an achieved status, and should be stated as such.

sections.heading: Master Reference — India's Status, Body by Body

rows: WHO / UNESCO / WTO / FAO / ILO / ICAO
Major shareholder / largest borrower (not founder in the historical sense; AIIB itself est. 2016)
Strategic partnership only (no membership category applies)
Aspirant (via G4), not an achieved status

quickRevision.oneLineDefinition: India is a founding member of the UN, IMF, World Bank, WHO, WTO, SAARC and BIMSTEC, a later-joining full member of the SCO (2017), and a partner (not member) of ASEAN, the OECD, and the EU.
keyFacts: Founding member: UN, IMF, World Bank, WHO, WTO/GATT, FAO, ILO, ICAO, SAARC, BIMSTEC, NDB.
Later full member (not founder): SCO (2017, alongside Pakistan).
Partner, not member: ASEAN (Dialogue Partner), OECD (Key Partner), EU/GCC/AU (Strategic Partnership only).
Hosts WHO's South-East Asia Regional Office (New Delhi) and the WHO Global Centre for Traditional Medicine (Jamnagar).
India is a UNSC permanent-seat ASPIRANT via the G4 (with Brazil, Germany, Japan) — not an achieved status.
commonConfusion: Being a major shareholder/borrower (AIIB) is not the same as being a treaty 'founding member' in the historical Bretton-Woods sense — keep these distinct in an answer.
India's UNSC permanent seat is a sought status, not a current fact — never state it as already achieved.

highYieldFacts: India: founding UN, IMF, World Bank, WHO, WTO/GATT member; founding SAARC and BIMSTEC member.
India joined SCO as a full member only in 2017 — not a founder (SCO est. 2001).
India is an ASEAN Dialogue Partner, NOT a full member — one of the most repeated exam traps in this whole subject.
commonTraps: Do not state India has a UNSC permanent seat — it is a candidate/aspirant via the G4, not a current member.
Do not conflate 'Key Partner' (OECD) or 'Dialogue Partner' (ASEAN) with full membership.
mustRemember: India's 1991 IMF loan is the fact most often linked to India's economic liberalization story.
India was declared polio-free by WHO in 2014.
possibleQuestions: Is India a founding member of the SCO? If not, when did it join?
What is India's official relationship status with the OECD?
